title: The Basie versus Lunceford battle of the bands in Hartford
summary: He switched bands the night of a Hartford battle of the bands and was interviewed on radio, praising both bands.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel

blocks.x: That's about right. And when I joined, the night I was supposed to join Lunceford, they booked the battle of music in Connecticut, something like that, -- no, a little further.
No, it must have been the other town, a little bigger than that. Stamford, I guess. What's that other town up there in Connecticut? Big, where they played a lot of dances.
The only place that I ever knew was the Ritz in Bridgeport.
No, it was another place, too, up there.
No, it was (inaudible). Bridgeport -- there's another town up there.

That's the town. And so they had me up there a day ahead of the concert. You know how they do those gimmicks, because they interviewed me on a radio program that day. Said, we got the man here that was with Basie three years ago, been with Lunceford and he's going back to Basie, and he's going to tell you what he thinks about how this battle is going to come out. One of them old Mohammed Ali things.
So they had me on and they asked me --
Oh, this was the night you joined Lunceford.
Yeah, this was the day before the night. I was finishing with Basie that night and joining Lunceford the next night. So the bands played a battle of the music, battle of the bands.

See, so that day they interviewed me about the difference in the bands. And they was trying to play up a big box office, so I made both bands the greatest bands in the world on each side, of this and that. And all

that and everything.

So that night, when Basie played his last tune, I think Lunceford -- no, Basie closed. And I had Basie's valet to come over and get my stuff and set it over on that side. So the promoters took advantage of it, because they had me on the air then, for about two hours on the program. Asked -- pumping questions about these two bands.

And you couldn't get anyplace. People tore the place up. They tore the place up.
